questions.q: What is the primary reason a designer might run out of time to complete a project?
options: Poor planning
Meeting warranty claims
Inappropriate target market
Late final payment from client
questions.explanation: Running out of time is a project-management failure: without action, time and finance plans, tasks are not sequenced or scheduled realistically. The other options affect a project but are not the primary cause of poor time control.

questions.q: What is the main goal of sustainable design?
options: To preserve the ozone layer
To reduce pollution and waste
To ensure the long-term availability of natural resources
To promote the responsible use of affordable materials by manufacturers
questions.explanation: Sustainability means meeting present needs without compromising the ability of future generations to meet theirs — i.e. the long-term availability of natural resources. Reducing pollution and waste is a means to that end, not the overarching goal.

questions.q: A designer has been asked to present a range of ideas for new greeting cards. What should the designer initially research in response to the brief?
options: Existing images and symbols
Strategies for product supply and distribution
Timelines and actions for product development
The value of instore gift cards to redeem for products
questions.explanation: At the ideation stage the designer researches the visual language of the product — existing images and symbols — to generate ideas. Supply, distribution and scheduling come later in the process, not at the initial research stage.

questions.q: What are the prime considerations for designers when producing safe and ethical products for consumers?
options: Social trends and convenience
Financial market share and existing products
Patent protection and niche market compatibility
End user wellbeing and environmental friendliness
questions.explanation: Safe and ethical design centres on the wellbeing of the end user and on minimising environmental harm. The other options are commercial or market considerations, not the prime safety/ethics considerations.

questions.q: Which of the following options best describes the features of a collaborative design team?
options: Leader directed, common skills among the group, responsive to feedback
Leader directed, various fields of professional expertise, responsive to feedback
Shared understanding of the project, common skills among the team, cooperative decision-making process
Shared understanding of the project, various fields of professional expertise, cooperative decision-making process
questions.explanation: A collaborative team shares a common understanding of the project, brings together varied fields of expertise, and makes decisions cooperatively rather than being directed by a single leader. Option D captures all three features.

questions.q: Which of the following is the most effective method to improve the design of new housing estates?
options: Limit the designers' creative freedom
Influence building regulations and land use policies
Mandate the use of specific brands of construction material
Require designers to prioritise ornate and decorative interior styles
questions.explanation: Regulations and land-use policies shape every estate at scale — setting standards for sustainability, safety and amenity. Limiting creativity or mandating brands/styles is narrow and counterproductive.

questions.q: A corporation has commissioned a designer to develop a new solar-powered, mobile interactive game. What is an ethical way to protect the intellectual property of the new design?
options: The designer applies for a patent.
The corporation applies for a patent.
The designer applies for copyright protection.
The corporation applies for copyright protection.
questions.explanation: A new functional invention (a solar-powered interactive device) is protected by a patent, not copyright. Because the corporation commissioned and owns the design, the corporation is the party that should apply for the patent.

questions.q: What is the most important reason for undertaking a life cycle analysis of an innovative design?
options: To establish the rights of the designer
To research the possibility of future growth in market share
To understand the impact of the project on society and the environment
To determine the level of consumer demand for the newly developed product
questions.explanation: A life cycle analysis traces a product from raw materials to disposal to reveal its impact on society and the environment across its whole life. The other options are commercial or legal aims, not the purpose of an LCA.

questions.q: When communicating to an audience, what is the best method of effectively transferring information?
options: Using language and technical jargon to impress the audience
Keeping the message simple to appeal to a broad range of people
Providing as much data as possible to cover all potential interests
Tailoring the message to address the needs and preferences of the audience
questions.explanation: Effective communication tailors the message to the specific needs and preferences of the audience. Jargon excludes people, over-simplifying loses meaning, and dumping all the data overwhelms rather than informs.

questions.q: A designer has been asked to analyse the ergonomic implications of a given task. What knowledge would the designer need to have to complete the analysis?
options: The cost-effectiveness of innovating work practices
The most common workplace injuries and their causes
The physical demands and human requirements for the job
The psychological wellbeing of employees in the workplace
questions.explanation: Ergonomics fits the task to the human body, so the analysis needs knowledge of the physical demands of the job and the physical requirements/capabilities of the user. Injuries and wellbeing are related outcomes, not the core ergonomic data.

questions.q:
An e-scooter is a battery-powered device that can be used for transportation or leisure activities.

Outline ONE factor of design that would be important in the development of an e-scooter.

criteria.descriptor: Outlines ONE factor that is important for the development of an e-scooter

questions.modelAnswer: Safety — the batteries used to store energy have been known to catch fire, so the designer must ensure that all possible safety precautions are taken in the e-scooter's design. (Other valid factors include function — it must be rideable; ergonomics — suited to the size and shape of the user; durability; obsolescence/safe disposal; and finance — cost-effective for the consumer.)

questions.q: Describe ONE disadvantage of designing a product with a limited life span.

criteria.descriptor: Demonstrates a thorough understanding of a disadvantage of designing a product with a limited lifespan
Demonstrates some understanding of a disadvantage of designing a product with a limited lifespan

questions.modelAnswer: A disposable plastic water bottle has a deliberately limited lifespan. Designing a product to become obsolete and need replacement raises an ethical concern and drives long-term environmental harm — consuming natural resources, adding to landfill and waste, and imposing ongoing financial cost on consumers who must keep re-buying it.

questions.q: Discuss ONE social trend that can affect the design of a new product.

criteria.descriptor: Discusses the effect of a social trend on the design of a new product
Demonstrates an understanding of a social trend that can affect the design of a new product
Demonstrates an understanding of a social trend

questions.modelAnswer: One social trend is the use of artificial intelligence. AI can generate images and concepts from written descriptions, which is a good way to stimulate design ideas — but the concept is not the designer's own work, raising authorship and intellectual-property issues. (Other trends worth discussing: eco/green materials, fast fashion and its waste, and the throw-away society of constant technology upgrades.)

questions.q: Explain ONE risk that a designer may face when creating an innovative product, system or environment. Provide an example to support your answer.

criteria.descriptor: Provides a thorough explanation of ONE risk involved in developing new designs; makes detailed reference to an innovation; provides a detailed example
Provides a sound explanation of ONE risk; makes reference to an innovation; provides an example
Provides a description of ONE risk a designer may experience; includes an example
Demonstrates some understanding of a risk a designer may experience in developing ideas

questions.modelAnswer: One major risk is that the innovative product fails to meet a real consumer need, costing money and damaging the brand. For example, while electric passenger cars are succeeding, electric recreational vehicles and utes have struggled because they cannot perform key functions — an EV ute has trouble towing a boat, making it impractical. The result is lost investment and negative brand identity, and some manufacturers are discontinuing these models. The risk is that the further a design pushes into the new and unproven, the greater the chance it misjudges what users actually require.

questions.q:
Stimulus — Examples of new discoveries and the role of the designer:

• Toothpaste — the designer created the packaging to bring the product to market.

Assess the role that a designer has in bridging the gap between new discoveries and the consumer market. Refer to the stimulus material in your response.

Your answer will be assessed on how well you: demonstrate knowledge and understanding relevant to the question; communicate ideas and information using relevant examples; and present a logical and cohesive response.

criteria.descriptor: Provides comprehensive assessment of the role a designer has in bridging the gap between new discoveries and the consumer market; logical and cohesive; relevant examples; detailed reference to ONE discovery from the stimulus
Provides a thorough assessment; logical and cohesive; relevant examples; reference to ONE discovery from the stimulus
Provides a sound assessment of the role of a designer; makes reference to a relevant example
Demonstrates some understanding of the role of a designer in bridging the gap between a discovery and the consumer market

questions.modelAnswer: Designers bridge the gap between a new discovery and the consumer market by turning a raw advance into a usable, desirable, marketable product. Using the stimulus: new toothpaste formulas were discovered, but it was designers who created accessible packaging, child-friendly flavours (and 'mint' as a cue for freshness), innovated the application through the electric toothbrush, and shifted from plastic to bamboo handles for sustainability — each design decision bringing the discovery to market and growing market share. The same role appears in the discovery of storing electrical power for cars: it only reached consumers because designers made it cost-effective and accessible, for example by designing charging-station networks so the cars remain viable and functional. A comprehensive assessment judges that without the designer translating discovery into a marketable, functional, appropriately-packaged product, many advances would never reach society at all — the designer is the essential link between invention and everyday use.
